messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected: elevated inference tail latency observed in production (p99 spike) for streaming endpoints. Alert rule: streaming_tail_latency_p99 > 2000ms (5m).
Mikaela Rivera: seeing this in dashboards now — p95 ~ 900ms, p99 ~ 5200ms across us-east region. Streaming stalls up to 18% of requests.
Raj Patel: I’m on it. Pulling recent deploys + cache telemetry. Any recent config changes to prefix hashing or cache invalidation?
Derek Chan: I rolled a small prefix-hash tweak 4h ago as part of rollout-42 (reduces collisions). It passed canary.
Luis Ortega: metrics: prefix cache hit rate dropped from 91% -> 36% in last 30m. KV bucket evictions spike aligned with the latency. Looks like new hash mapping caused hot-shard skew and high miss rate.
Sara Nguyen: confirmed customer reports. Customer-ops: two large customers reported timeouts and degraded streaming. No billing impact yet but UX broken.
Mikaela Rivera: immediate mitigations we can try: 1) revert prefix-hash rollout, 2) enable prefetched cold-cache warmup for high-qps prefixes, 3) increase per-shard memory reservation temporarily. Thoughts?
Raj Patel: revert first. If hash mapping is the root cause, revert should restore hit rate quickly. I’ll trigger rollback of rollout-42 to prior hash mapping.
Derek Chan: on it. Rolling back rollout-42 now. Command: ```./deployctl rollback --feature prefix-hash --to-tag rollout-41``` 
oncall-bot: deployctl: rollback started by Derek Chan (id: rb-20260315-01). ETA ~ 3m per region for config propagation.
Luis Ortega: while rollback runs, adding emergency TTL bump for prefix-cache keys so slightly older entries stay valid: ```redis-cli -h cache-prod -a *** EVAL "for k in redis.call('keys', ARGV[1]) do redis.call('expire', k, tonumber(ARGV[2])) end" 0 "prefix:*" 120``` — applying to us-east first.
Sara Nguyen: enabling fallback path for streaming to use dedicated inference pool (slightly higher cost) to reduce end-user timeouts. Toggle: `feature-toggle streaming-dedicated-fallback on`
Mikaela Rivera: good. Can someone watch p99 and hit-rate as rollback finishes? Raj + Luis?
Raj Patel: watching. Initial signals: pre-rollback p99 5200ms, median 200ms. Cache hit rate dropping correlated with specific prefix set: customer_bindings/* and shared-prompts/* are the worst.
Luis Ortega: rollback propagated in us-east1. Cache hit rate up to 68% within 90s post-rollback for affected prefixes. p99 falling to ~1200ms.
Derek Chan: rollback complete across all regions. Rollback ID rb-20260315-01 finished. No errors in logs.
oncall-bot: Deploy event: rollback completed by Derek Chan (id: rb-20260315-01).
Mikaela Rivera: telemetry update: us-east p99 now ~980ms, p95 ~420ms. Streaming stalls down to 6%. Still above SLO but trending down.
Raj Patel: digging into why canary didn't catch this. Canary had synthetic traffic with even distribution; production has skew (heavy tail of long prefixes). Canary workload lacked those hot prefixes. Need to add targeted patterns to canary.
Derek Chan: also saw increased KV eviction rates on nodes 7-9 indicating skew. Adding auto-replicas for hot keys as short-term relief. Command: `kvadmin scale --nodes 7,8,9 --replicas 2`
Luis Ortega: hotkey replication applied. Hit rate for customer_bindings/* now 85% for replicated nodes. p99 down to 560ms.
Sara Nguyen: customer-ops updated customers in the impacted cohort: 2 customers still reporting intermittent stalls (20% of their sessions). They're on shared prefix namespace.
Mikaela Rivera: action items before handoff: 1) postmortem owner, 2) revert rollout noted and link to changelist, 3) add targeted canary tests for hot prefixes, 4) review prefix-hash algorithm for skew edgecases, 5) capacity plan for cache to avoid single-shard hot spots.
Raj Patel: I’ll own the postmortem and analysis of canary gaps. Tracking ticket: #INC-2026-prefix-skew (create after thread).
Derek Chan: I’ll follow up with a small patch to enforce uniform bucket mapping for known high-qps namespaces and add auto-rollback on hit-rate drop threshold.
Luis Ortega: I’ll write a short runbook for oncall: if prefix cache hit rate drops >20% in 10m, do an automated revert and enable hotkey replication.
Sara Nguyen: customer-ops: sending proactive comms to affected customers with ETA for full recovery (~2h) and a short explanation. Keeping them updated.
oncall-bot: Reminder: create incident record with severity and impacted customers.
Mikaela Rivera: current status summary for handoff: root cause likely faulty prefix-hash rollout causing heavy shard skew -> massively increased cache misses -> increased backend load and streaming tail latency. Mitigations executed: rollback rollout-42, TTL bump, hotkey replication, enable streaming-dedicated-fallback. User impact limited to degraded streaming UX and elevated latencies for some customers.
Mikaela Rivera: handing off to night oncall (Raj will stay on for 15m to ensure stability then hand to Derek). Raj, please add any more context in the incident ticket and include the exact changelist.
Raj Patel: will do. I’ll stay 15m, then hand to Derek. Post-rollback checks: p99 steady ~480-620ms, hit rate ~88% overall.
Derek Chan: acknowledged — will pick up and run through the runbook overnight. If anything regresses, escalate to infra oncall and PM.
Sara Nguyen: thanks team. Sending out customer note and internal summary. :white_check_mark:
Mikaela Rivera: thanks everyone. Logging the timeline and attaching brief graphs to the incident ticket.
customer-ops: noted — we’ll follow up with customers once you confirm full resolution.
Mikaela Rivera: Incident severity: Sev2 (user-facing latency and degraded SLAs). Postmortem owner: Raj Patel. Handoff complete.
